_meta.what: When each municipal corporation was constituted, under which Act, and from which lineage. The 74th Amendment (1992) is the measuring stick: most of these bodies are FAR older than the Amendment that was supposed to finally empower them — and the powers were hollowed out (water boards, development authorities, SPVs) regardless of how venerable the corporation is.
_meta.fields: municipality_year = first municipal body; corporation_year = constituted as a Municipal CORPORATION (the empowered, mayor-led body); corporation_act = the governing statute; lineage = presidency_capital | bombay_presidency_bpmc | princely_state | provincial_other; improvement_trust = the colonial/early land body (Ghosh's 'improvement regime'); development_authority = its modern successor that holds planning/land OUTSIDE the elected corporation.
_meta.status: Assembled 2026-06 from the legislative record + AMC's official history + Anwesha Ghosh, 'Municipal Calcutta' (UofT PhD, 2021) and 'The Improvement Regime' (CSSH, 2025). verify:true = year/Act to be confirmed against the statute. NOT fabricated — uncertain entries are flagged, not guessed silently.
_meta.key_finding: Three lineages. (1) PRESIDENCY CAPITALS — Madras (1688, the oldest corporation in India), Calcutta (1726 JPs → 1876/1923), Bombay (1888) — got the earliest, strongest corporations. (2) BOMBAY-PRESIDENCY cities under the BPMC Act 1949 — Ahmedabad, Pune, Surat (and Baroda/Nagpur by absorption) — inherited that strong-corporation template. (3) PRINCELY-STATE capitals — Hyderabad, Bangalore (Mysore), Jaipur, Cochin — had separate municipal genealogies. Devolution today does NOT track age: Madras is oldest yet scores 50%; the divergence comes from the POST-1960s parastatal carve-out, not the founding.

ahmedabad.corporation_act: Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 (inherited by Gujarat 1960; renamed the GPMC Act)

proto_origin.name: Town Wall Fund Committee
proto_origin.note: 1% cess on ghee etc. to repair the flood-damaged fort wall — the seed of municipal taxation

ahmedabad.notes: AMC's own claim: 'the first people's representative council in India' — a claim about ELECTED self-government (1915), distinct from the oldest CORPORATION (Madras 1688). Town-planning tradition runs through the Bombay Town Planning Act, 1915, not a separate improvement trust.

mumbai.corporation_act: Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 (still in force; governs MCGM)
mumbai.notes: The 1888 Act is one of the strongest, most enduring municipal statutes in India — it gives BMC capacious in-house powers (water, sewerage, transport via BEST, hospitals). The Bombay Improvement Trust (1898), formed after the 1896 plague, is the prototype Ghosh analyses for the 'improvement regime'.
sources: Kidambi, The Making of an Indian Metropolis (2007)

chennai.corporation_act: Royal Charter, 29 September 1688 (East India Company); later the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919
chennai.notes: THE OLDEST municipal corporation in India (Corporation of Madras, 1688) — older than every other on this list by two centuries. The central irony of the atlas: the oldest corporation is among the MOST hollowed (water → Metrowater 1978, planning → CMDA 1972, transport → MTC). Age did not protect devolution.

kolkata.corporation_act: 1876 (Bengal Act); the foundational Calcutta Municipal Act, 1923; renamed under the Calcutta Municipal Corporation Act, 1980
kolkata.notes: Municipal authority from the 1726 Charter (Justices of the Peace); corporate form 1876; the 1923 Act (associated with C.R. Das) widened the franchise. This is the city of Ghosh's thesis: the municipality as 'a corporate body … like the joint stock company,' biased toward 'economically gainful projects' — the colonial regime of property and the 'landlord-entrepreneur'.

pune.corporation_act: Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 (constituted 15 February 1950)
pune.notes: The clean tell of the Bombay-Presidency family: PMC was incorporated under the SAME 1949 Act as Ahmedabad, weeks apart in 1950. Keeps water and sewerage in-house.

surat.corporation_act: Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 (as the GPMC Act in Gujarat)
surat.notes: Same GPMC Act as Ahmedabad. SMC is India's most-cited well-run corporation — the in-house service-delivery turnaround after the 1994 plague. Not yet in the atlas's city set; included here because it proves devolution is set by the STATE's law (GPMC), not the individual city.

vadodara.corporation_act: Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 (after Baroda State merged into Bombay, 1949)
vadodara.notes: Baroda was a PRINCELY state (Gaekwad), NOT Bombay Presidency — but it merged into Bombay state in 1949 and so inherited the BPMC/GPMC Act anyway. A neat case of how the Bombay legal template spread by absorption. Not yet in the atlas's city set.

bengaluru.corporation_act: City of Bangalore Municipal Corporation Act, 1949; BBMP (Greater Bangalore) constituted 2007
bengaluru.notes: Princely Mysore lineage. The CITB (1945) → BDA (1976) is a textbook improvement-trust-to-development-authority succession: land and planning sit OUTSIDE the elected BBMP. Water went to BWSSB (1964). The 2024 Greater Bengaluru Governance Act further splits BBMP itself.
sources: City of Bangalore Municipal Corporation Act 1949

hyderabad.corporation_act: Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad (MCH), 1955; GHMC constituted 2007
hyderabad.notes: Princely Hyderabad (Nizam) lineage; the city had its own municipal and improvement bodies under the Nizam before accession (1948). Water → HMWSSB (1989).

visakhapatnam.notes: Madras-Presidency district (municipality 1858 is genuinely old, contemporaneous with Pune), but the CORPORATION form came late (1979). Keeps water in-house (GVMC).

development_authority.name: KDA (Kanpur Development Authority)
development_authority.note: under the UP Urban Planning & Development Act 1973; successor to the 1919 Improvement Trust

kanpur.notes: United Provinces lineage. Cawnpore had an early improvement trust (1919) — an industrial-city version of the same improvement regime. Water/sewerage hived to Jal Sansthan / UP Jal Nigam.

jaipur.corporation_act: Rajasthan Municipalities Act (corporation form post-74th Amendment, 1994); split into Greater + Heritage corporations, 2019
jaipur.notes: Princely Jaipur (Kachhwaha) lineage. The CORPORATION is recent (1994) and weak: JDA (1982) and PHED hold most of the land, roads and water a corporation elsewhere would run. Among the least devolved.

bhubaneswar.notes: India's first major POST-independence planned capital (Otto Königsberger plan, 1948). The development authority (BDA, 1983) predates the municipal corporation (1994) — the planned city was run by the planners before it was ever given an elected council. Water sits with WATCO/state.

kochi.corporation_act: Corporation of Cochin, 1967 (merger of Fort Cochin, Mattancherry, Ernakulam and others under the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act)
kochi.notes: A composite lineage: Fort Cochin was Madras-Presidency, Mattancherry/Ernakulam were princely Cochin/Travancore. Unified as one corporation only in 1967. Kerala's strong municipal-law regime (ASICS-rated highest) coexists with most utilities at the state level (KWA water, KSEB power).

development_authority.name: Nagpur Improvement Trust (NIT)
development_authority.note: a RARE surviving improvement TRUST — the very body type Ghosh studies, still operating as the planning authority alongside NMC

nagpur.notes: Central Provinces & Berar lineage. Nagpur is the live museum specimen of the improvement regime: the NIT (1936) never became a 'development authority' — it is still called a Trust and still runs planning/land beside the elected NMC.
